findings.original: not only value, but at the same time surplus-value.
findings.rewrite: and not only value, but surplus-value at the same time.
findings.problem: First technical use of surplus-value in Ch. 7 body text (ch07-s1 had it only in headings) gets no §7 explanation, though the term is not defined by Marx here.
findings.fix: Append the §7 wording: "…but surplus-value at the same time (surplus-value is the extra value that workers produce beyond the value of their own labor-power, which the capitalist keeps without paying for it)."

findings.original: that its subject is cotton and its product yarn, than we are about the fact that the subject itself is already a product … the subject of his labour, the coal
findings.rewrite: that its subject is cotton, and that its product is yarn, than we are with the fact that the subject itself is already a product … the subject of his labor, the coal
findings.problem: "subject of labour" (the material worked on) must be rendered "object of labor" per the Phase 4 glossary entry and ch07-s1's usage.
findings.fix: Replace the three occurrences with "its object is cotton", "the object itself", "the object of his labor".

notes_review: Sound overall: the capitalist's invented speeches keep their tags and the mocked words ('abstinence', 'service'), and the n. 13 French retranslation and n. 18 figures are handled correctly; declining §7 glosses where Marx defines the term himself (socially necessary labor-time, value of labor-power, metamorphosis as money-into-capital) is right. The notes omitted surplus-value, which ch07-s1 had explicitly passed on; 'wages' and 'proletariat' have no technical use in this file (only inside Olmsted's quotation), so no explanation is owed in Ch. 7.
summary: Fidelity is high: no lost or added claims, the irony of the capitalist's dialogue and the 'eternal laws' scare quotes survive, and all figures match. Readability is good; the only problems were a missing first-use surplus-value explanation and three leftover 'subject of labor' renderings.
